name: Yellowish camel
lede: Yellowish camel is ColorHub's English name for Shirotsurubami, a traditional Japanese color meaning "white oak," and one of the most common tans in our painting archive.

sections.title: White oak
sections.body:
白橡 (Shirotsurubami) literally means white oak, part of a Japanese family of oak-based browns that also includes the darker [[yellowish-hazel]] [1]. ColorHub renders it as Yellowish camel for English readers; the name is a fair guide, since the library's nearest standard name is Camel itself [1][2].

In the look-alike data, [[cinnamon-buff]] sits closest at 2.8 units, almost the same; [[camel]] follows at 3.1, and [[peachbeige]] at 3.8 [2]. [[cinnamon]], 4.2 units off, reads more vivid [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: It is one of the more common names we track, found in 8.13 percent of 23,781 paintings, 1,934 of them as photographed, more common than 92 percent of the colors in our archive [3]. The Master of Alkmaar used it most intensely, in 5 of 13 works here, 4.7 times that collection's baseline [3]. It peaks in the 1500s, found in 7.8 percent of the 2,231 paintings we have from then, 173 of them, 1.5 times the expected rate, and plays an accent in 46 percent of its paintings [3]. It is most over-represented in paintings from India, 2.8 times expected, and tends to share canvases with Deep Champagne and Cork more than chance would predict [3].
